response: Yes, lower fasting plasma glucose levels at diagnosis of type 2 diabetes are associated with improved outcomes. Research has shown that individuals with type 2 diabetes who have lower fasting plasma glucose levels at diagnosis tend to have better health outcomes, including reduced risk of complications such as cardiovascular disease, kidney disease, and retinopathy. Additionally, lower fasting plasma glucose levels at diagnosis are also associated with improved survival rates and reduced need for medications or insulin therapy. Early detection and treatment of type 2 diabetes, when glucose levels are still relatively low, can help prevent or delay the onset of these complications, leading to improved overall health outcomes.
